subject: Discrepancies in Usage Claims and SaaS Entitlement Granularity
messages:
From: Acme Billing <acct-billing@acme-corp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected charges — marketplace fulfillment vs contract entitlements

Hi Vanessa,

We ran our monthly invoice reconciliation and see a ~12% delta between what AWS Marketplace billed and the entitlements in our signed SaaS contract (SKU ACME-REDWOOD-ENT). Specifically, we received usage records that appear to have been measured at a finer granularity (token-hours) while our contract is seat-based with monthly caps. The result is overage line items that don't match our agreed limits.

Attached: usage-log-payloads.csv (sample of marketplace metering records for Apr 15–25).

Can you help reconcile where the mapping between marketplace "usageDimension" and our contract entitlement is happening? We need a short joint plan to either reclassify those claims or get credit adjustments.

Thanks — Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Cloud Finance, Acme Analytics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Billing <acct-billing@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges — marketplace fulfillment vs contract entitlements

Jane — thanks for the heads up and for the sample file. We take billing mismatches seriously.

Quick summary of next steps we propose:
- Ben and Karthik will triage the payloads to identify whether records were sent under the wrong meteringDimension or if fulfillment transformed the SKU at ingestion.
- I'll loop in AWS Marketplace partner support to validate if a known fulfillment bug could drop or remap entitlement identifiers on batched events.
- We'll produce a reconciliation CSV with proposed adjustments and a one-time credit if the fault is on our fulfillment pipeline.
- If we need an amendment for entitlement granularity (seat vs token-hours) we'll prepare a short DocuSign amendment for your review.

Can you confirm a preferred cut-off window for the reconciliation (we suggest Apr 1–25) and whether a settlement credit applied to May invoice is acceptable?

[Attachment: initial-recon-request.md] (outline of fields we need)

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Director, Partnerships & Marketplace, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Acme Billing <acct-billing@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges — marketplace fulfillment vs contract entitlements

Thanks Jane — I pulled the sample payloads and a few things stand out:

1) Metering dimension mismatch: Some records show usageDimension="token_hours" while the product in our storefront is registered under SKU=ACME-REDWOOD-ENT with dimension="seats". AWS allows custom dimensions, but the fulfillment flow is expected to map the marketplace usage to the SKU-level entitlement during entitlement creation; that mapping appears to be missing for ~8% of events.

2) Webhook processing errors: We see repeated 500 responses from our fulfillment callback between Apr 16 02:14–02:27 UTC — those failures caused retry windows and, in a few cases, duplicate claims after replay. See stubbed error: [Attachment: fulfillment-error-500.json].

3) Idempotency & replay: Some upstream events are missing a stable idempotencyKey; replays therefore generate additional usage events with slightly different meta (e.g., instance_id vs customer_id).

Temporary mitigation options I recommend:
- Patch our fulfillment listener to normalize incoming dimension names (map token_hours -> seats_equiv via a conversion factor) and drop events without a canonical entitlement_id.
- For the repayment window, produce an adjustments file that groups by customer_sku and time bucket, then apply credit reversals for duplicates.

I'll prepare a recon-adjustments-proposal.csv with the grouped corrections and the suggested credit amounts. Ben

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: AWS Marketplace Support <aws-partner@amazon.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Acme Billing <acct-billing@acme-corp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 07:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Unexpected charges — marketplace fulfillment vs contract entitlements (AMZ-11234)

Hi team,

We investigated case AMZ-11234 and confirmed there is a known regression in the SaaS fulfillment path when a product has both a custom usageDimension and a storefront SKU with seat-based entitlements. Batched usage events where the productCode did not exactly match the registered product code sometimes fall back to a generic dimension and create separate usage lines. The issue was most active on Apr 15–18 and was patched on Apr 20.

What we need from you: a list of the exact productCode values in the events you received and timestamps for the failed webhooks so we can correlate with our logs. We can also issue a retroactive correction for marketplace billing if AWS-side attribution is shown to be in error — however, AWS requires a reconciliation CSV with the following columns: productCode, licenseIdentifier, timestampUTC, recordedQuantity, correctedQuantity, justification.

Link to case: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/AMZ-11234

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Partner Support

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Billing <acct-billing@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Support <aws-partner@amazon.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RE: Unexpected charges — marketplace fulfillment vs contract entitlements (AMZ-11234)

Jane — forwarding AWS's confirmation. We ran the grouping script and attached a proposed adjustments CSV with the clustered corrections and suggested credit amounts in the last column. If you approve, we'll: 1) submit the reconciliation CSV to AWS with the supporting logs, 2) apply internal credit reversals for any duplicates we generated on our side, and 3) push a small contract amendment clarifying mapping for token->seat equivalence for any future metering.

Please confirm:
- Cut-off window: Apr 1–25 (we used that range)
- Settlement preference: apply credit to May invoice (yes/no)
- Whether Acme wants Redwood to submit the AWS reconciliation on your behalf or you will do it.

[Attachment: recon-adjustments-proposal.csv]

Thanks Vanessa and team — the plan sounds good.

Confirming:
- Cut-off window: Apr 1–25 OK.
- Apply credit to May invoice — yes.
- Please submit the reconciliation CSV to AWS on behalf of Acme; we authorize Redwood to act as our integration point for this issue.

We'd like the reconciliation to include the original marketplace event ids for audit purposes. Once we receive the proposed credit amounts I'll approve them and sign the amendment if it clarifies future dimension mapping.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Jane
